proposition: Under the map n -> n/2 when n is even, n -> 3n+1 when n is odd, every integer n with 1 <= n <= 39087 reaches 1 in fewer than 276 steps.
hypotheses: the stopping time counts steps until the value 1 is reached

argument.text: For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, (n-3)*(n^2) equals (n-3)*((n^2) + [n = 3]).
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000 for which n^2 > 666.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, n^3 is congruent to (n^3) + 91 modulo 7.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, if n mod 4 = 0 then (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000 for which n^3 > 500.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2316, the stopping time of n is less than 276.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, n^3 + n is congruent to (n^3 + n) + 69 modulo 23.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, at least one of the following holds: n mod 2 = 0; n mod 2 = 1.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 50, the stopping time of n is less than 276.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, (n-4)*(n*(n+1)) equals (n-4)*((n*(n+1)) + [n = 4]).
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, n^2 is at least n.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, at least one of the following holds: n mod 4 = 0; n mod 4 = 1; n mod 4 = 2; n mod 4 = 3.
For every integer n with 2 <= n <= 2000, n^3 is at least 3*n.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 2000, if n mod 2 = 1 then (n^2) mod 2 = 1.
The steps above establish the statement up to 2316, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 39087.
